newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Death toll rises to 11 as Philippine ferry sinks.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to 11 as Philippine ferry sinks.

text.p: Rescue workers fished out 11 bodies and were searching for at least 20 others in the Samar Sea in the central Philippines after an inter-island ferry sank early on Friday.

They earlier rescued 51 survivors from the Kalibo Star, which went under in strong winds and high seas off Biliran province, 480 km (298 miles) south of Manila, said Carlo Centinage, duty officer at the regional disaster office.
He added that the weather had since cleared, enabling rescuers to scour the area.
Survivors were rescued by fishermen and police boats that were patrolling the area, known to be infested by sharks.
Those dead included nine women, a two-year-old girl and a man.
Centinage said the Coast Guard was investigating the accident.

Based on the manifest, there were 52 passengers and 30 crew members en route to Tacloban from central Cebu city. But Centinage said the manifest might not have given the exact number of passengers on board.
Crew members said the vessel could accommodate more than 400 passengers and was therefore not overloaded.
